title: a `neural_block` exec reference carrying an unrecognized third key is rejected (the object is CLOSED)
why: An exec ref's wire shape is fixed to exactly
`{'kind': ..., 'kernel': ...}` — before this hardening a third key (a digest
payload, a stray typo) passed validation silently in BOTH languages, because
`_validate_exec_ref` only ever READ `kind`/`kernel` off the object and never
checked its key set. This row closes that gap: the object is now CLOSED, not
merely SHAPED — an unrecognized key is refused by name.
Fixture content is row01's golden with one field changed (`forward_exec` grows a
third key, `digest`) — the ONLY thing that can make it reject is the closure
check under test; `forward_exec.kind`/`forward_exec.kernel` and the untouched
`vjp_exec` stay valid, so a validator that still only reads the two known keys
would accept this fixture and fail the row.
The C++ half parses the exec-ref object's TOP-LEVEL keys at parse time
(`_object_keys`, `plugin/sidecar.h`) and carries any unrecognized ones on
validation-free, like every other field the scanner reads, matching the
parse/validate split the rest of the header already follows.
`host_add_plugin` is exercised too: its only structural gate is the shared
validator, so the check must live there, not in a per-loader afterthought.
